sentences.text: Xixiasaurus henanensis is the only known species of this theropod dinosaur, which belongs to the family Troodontidae.
The single known fossil includes an almost complete skull missing its rear section, along with a partial right forelimb and some jaw fragments.
Scientists estimated this animal to be about 1.5 meters long and to weigh roughly 8 kilograms.
It differed from other members of its group by having a downturned front end of the lower jaw that resembled a chin-like eminence found in therizinosaurian theropods.
Because the nasal bones of the holotype were not fused, researchers believe the individual may not have been fully mature.
The dinosaur possessed a unique chin-like structure on its lower jaw that was not seen in other troodontids.
The unfused nasal bones suggest the holotype specimen was likely a juvenile rather than an adult.
The genus was formally named by Lü and colleagues in the year 2010.
The holotype specimen, catalogued as HGM 41HIII-0201, was discovered near Songgou Village in Xixia County, Henan Province.
Troodontids, including Xixiasaurus, possessed some of the highest encephalization quotients among non-avian dinosaurs, indicating a large brain relative to body size.
Large eye sockets and a well-developed middle ear suggest these animals had keen senses.
Proportionally long legs indicate that troodontids were agile creatures.
Researchers suggest the lack of serrated teeth indicates Xixiasaurus was herbivorous, as it had lost the ability to cut meat.

In 1998, Thomas R. Holtz and colleagues noted that troodontid tooth serrations were large and widely spaced, resembling those of herbivorous dinosaurs and lizards rather than typical carnivorous theropods.
Due to large brains, possible stereoscopic vision, grasping hands, and enlarged sickle-shaped claws, troodontids were generally assumed to be predators.
Xixiasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 86 million years ago during the Santonian age in what is now Asia.
Fossils are found in the Majiacun Formation, whose exact age remains uncertain.
Lü and colleagues suggested the Majiacun Formation dates to the Campanian age based on similarities between Xixiasaurus and the Campanian genus Byronosaurus.
These sedimentary rocks were deposited by braided streams and meandering streams and are characterized by containing abundant dinosaur eggs.

There is an ongoing debate regarding whether troodontids like Xixiasaurus were carnivorous, omnivorous, or herbivorous. In 2001, Philip J. Currie and Dong Zhiming rejected the hypothesis that troodontids were herbivorous. In 2015, Christophe Hendrickx and colleagues proposed that basal troodontids with unserrated teeth were herbivores, while derived troodontids with serrated teeth were carnivores or omnivores.
